clue.text: Wood, we hear, with sound colour and tone

indicators.note: says the word for wood is to be heard rather than spelt, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: timber is wood cut for building

explanation.surface: A musician describes a wooden instrument's voice in terms of colour and tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbre is the distinctive quality of a musical sound, often called tone colour, separate from pitch and loudness.

clue.text: Trains one to go out and do a deal

indicators.note: the letter for one leaves the word, so it is removed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Railway trains leave one station to complete a business deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To transact is to conduct business, to deal with someone in a trade.

clue.text: Custom in rent calculation that's wrong

indicators.note: rent here means torn apart, so the letters are torn up and reordered

explanation.surface: A habitual way of working out rent turns out to give the wrong figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money paid for housing; it is the past tense of rend, to tear.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscount is an incorrect count, a reckoning that has gone wrong.

clue.text: Go back to square one when New Street's not finished

indicators.note: new letters means the remaining ones are made into a fresh arrangement
the word's final letter is left off, as if it were incomplete

parts.note: the word street, with the apostrophe s as is

explanation.surface: A road-builder must start again because New Street is incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: New Street looks like a place name, but 'New' is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset something is to return it to its starting state, like going back to the beginning of a board game.

clue.text: Not deviating when attracted to the opposite sex

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are joined by 'when', which only links them.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both going in a direct line without curving and, informally, heterosexual.

clue.text: Way to solve a problem of hearing with inaccuracy

parts.note: a trial is a court hearing
and joins one thing with another

explanation.surface: A deaf person's difficulty with mistakes is treated as a problem to be solved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' suggests a sound, but it is the legal sense, a case in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Trial and error is the method of solving something by attempting options and learning from failures.

clue.text: Say topless bikini, for example, gets pained expression from cleric

indicators.note: the word loses its top, its first letter

parts.note: Bikini is a Pacific atoll, famous for nuclear tests
ah is an exclamation of pain

explanation.surface: A Muslim cleric winces at the sight of a topless bikini.
explanation.walkthrough: The bikini swimsuit was named after Bikini Atoll in the Marshall Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: An ayatollah is a senior religious leader among Shiite Muslims, especially in Iran.

clue.text: Professional entertainer of his age? Ridiculous!

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in an absurd way, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of a hostess being his age.
explanation.definitionFit: A geisha is a Japanese woman trained to entertain guests with music, dance and conversation.

clue.text: Rent rise includes an old coin

indicators.note: the reversed word takes the other word inside it
in a down clue the word rent goes upwards, read backwards

explanation.surface: A rent increase is reckoned to include an old coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A tanner was the old British sixpence, before decimal coinage in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanner is British slang for a sixpenny piece, a coin no longer in use.

clue.text: Fools the girls when student drops out

indicators.note: the student leaves the group of girls, so that letter is removed

parts.note: lasses are girls or young women
L is the learner plate, a crossword student

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that the young women are fools once a student quits the course.
explanation.definitionFit: Asses are stupid people, a standard synonym for fools.

clue.text: Feverishness led to it again having treatment

indicators.note: letters given treatment are worked over and rearranged, like a patient being treated

explanation.surface: A patient's fever returned, so they needed treatment again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feverishness' looks medical, but here it means nervous excitement rather than a temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitation is a state of nervous excitement or restlessness, which feverishness also describes.

clue.text: Awful rift with team-mate getting duck — it had to happen eventually

indicators.note: an awful mess of letters is reordered

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, the shape of O

explanation.surface: A cricketer falls out with a team-mate after scoring nothing, which was always coming.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes something certain to occur sooner or later, only the timing being uncertain.

clue.text: It's not enough to have a brief tumble!

explanation.surface: A quick fall is hardly worth mentioning, the exclamation jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortfall is a deficit, an amount by which something falls short of what is needed.

clue.text: Colouring chore, perhaps

indicators.note: suggests the word is only one possible arrangement of these letters, so they are mixed

explanation.surface: Colouring-in is described as a tedious household job.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy yellow-brown pigment used to colour paints.

clue.text: Reasonably, only half finally consent to sit around inside

indicators.note: this half of only is placed at the very end
the jumbled sitting word is placed within the word consent
the letters of sit are turned around into a new order
only the second half of the word only is kept

explanation.surface: Someone grudgingly agrees, only halfway, to sit about indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting consistently means acting in a steady, logical way, which is a loose synonym for reasonably.

clue.text: Cruelly revealed: fashionable person's ugly half

parts.note: a human is a person; the apostrophe s is the possessive surface

indicators.note: only the second half of the word ugly is kept

explanation.surface: A fashionable person's nasty side is exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting inhumanly means acting without compassion, which is behaving cruelly.

clue.text: Extrovert going out to change places

indicators.note: the two words swap order, so the second comes first

explanation.surface: An extrovert going out to try a change of scene.
explanation.definitionFit: An outgoing person is sociable and friendly, the same as an extrovert.

clue.text: Aware of having dispatched one to hospital department

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: Someone learns they have been referred to a hospital department.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentient means able to perceive or feel things, conscious and aware.

clue.text: Hire a home as monastery

parts.note: to charter is to hire a vehicle or vessel

explanation.surface: Someone rents a house to use as a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: A Charterhouse is a Carthusian monastery; the London one later became a school and almshouse.

clue.text: Discover if a far-off tree produces fibre

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or bad, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: Finding out whether a distant tree yields a useful fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'far-off' reads as one word meaning distant; split it and 'off' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffia is fibre from the leaves of the raffia palm, used for weaving baskets and mats.

clue.text: Her new Indian assistant originally diagnosing rupture

indicators.note: each of these words gives its original, first letter

explanation.surface: A new assistant from India diagnoses a patient's rupture.
explanation.definitionFit: A hernia is a medical rupture in which an organ pushes through the muscle wall containing it.

clue.text: Opposite the middle, find sailor, first engineer, in the morning

indicators.note: only the opening letter of engineer is used

explanation.surface: Instructions to track down a sailor and an engineer early in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeam is a nautical term for a position at right angles to a ship's keel, level with its middle.

clue.text: Could be lighter, if seen in the glow from the hearth

indicators.note: the letters could be arranged as something else, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: The room would be brighter if someone looked into the fireplace's glow.
explanation.definitionFit: Firelight is the illumination given off by a fire in a grate.

clue.text: Hostelry serving light food, it's said

indicators.note: spoken aloud the low-calorie word gives the answer

parts.note: low-cal food is low in calories

explanation.surface: A pub that serves diet meals.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain your local is the pub nearest your home that you regularly drink in.

clue.text: He pays for fine French article on cooked rice

parts.note: fin is the French word for fine or delicate

indicators.note: the rice is cooked up, its letters stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A man pays for a fine French dish served on rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' suggests F, but it needs 'French' with it.
explanation.definitionFit: A financier is a person who provides funding for ventures, the one who pays for them.

clue.text: No time for metric conversion when there's foul play

indicators.note: the remaining letters are converted into a new arrangement
says there is no room for this letter, so it is removed

explanation.surface: A complaint that there is no time to convert to metric measures, as though it were a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Foul play is an idiom for criminal or violent wrongdoing, a crime.

clue.text: Somehow lean, say, slightly at first, towards detailed tests

indicators.note: the letters are put together in some other way, signalling a rearrangement
only the opening letter of slightly is taken

explanation.surface: A vague remark about leaning slightly towards thorough examinations.
explanation.definitionFit: Analyses are close examinations of something in detail, such as laboratory tests.

clue.text: Curse second-class illumination!

parts.note: B is a second grade, after A

explanation.surface: Someone swears at a poor-quality lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A blight is a plague or affliction, something that spoils things, as a curse does.
